page: Amazon Web Services m6gd.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by 64 physical cores of the 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Built without a hypervisor, it provides direct access to 64 dedicated execution threads alongside 256 GB of DDR4 system memory, reflecting a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server includes 3,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers a 25 Gbps baseline network throughput. Hardware accelerators such as dedicated GPUs are not present on this instance type.

Benchmark data highlights strong performance in multi-threaded and I/O-intensive workloads. The server demonstrates high throughput in parallel code compilation with Clang, stress-ng multi-core evaluation, and cached memory bandwidth. In network and in-memory key-value processing, it achieves 79.92 million Redis SET operations per second and 47.27 GB per second in static web serving throughput. Conversely, single-threaded processing presents a clear tradeoff: Geekbench single-core, single-threaded gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression fall into lower performance brackets due to modest single-core clock speeds and arm64 architectural profiles. Similarly, large language model inference throughput remains low without specialized vector extensions or GPU acceleration.

With its dense physical core topology, balanced memory allocation, and large bundled NVMe storage tier, AWS m6gd.metal offers solid resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for scaled multi-threaded applications. The absence of hypervisor overhead combined with local high-speed storage makes the instance well matched for high-concurrency microservices, container hosts, distributed NoSQL databases, caching tiers, continuous integration build farms, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m6gd.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server featuring 64 physical cores on the 64-bit ARM Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 architecture at 2.5 GHz. It integrates 256 GB of DDR4 system memory, 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, and a 25 Gbps baseline network interface without hypervisor virtualization or GPU accelerators. Benchmark results reflect strong multi-threaded execution, high cached memory bandwidth, and high throughput in Redis operations and static web serving, alongside fast Clang compilation speeds. Single-thread performance and LLM inference generation remain lower due to moderate per-core clock frequency and the absence of specialized tensor instruction sets. The server profile is optimized for multi-threaded workloads, container infrastructure, distributed databases, caching tiers, and CI/CD compilation pipelines.
